closed_since: 2026-02-24 (令和8年2月24日) — final day of business, announced on a notice posted at the shop front
name: 粋な一生（いきないっしょう）
address_ja: 東京都台東区台東1-27-2 竹善ビル 1F
cuisine: A twenty-year neighbourhood ramen shokudō doing the three classics — shōyu, shio and miso — with the shio and the miso the ones regulars came for; miso ramen ¥900, butter and corn ¥120 each, sub-¥1,000 bowls. It shut for good on 24 February 2026.
neighborhood: Taitō 1-chōme, on the Taitō-ku side of the Chiyoda boundary — cross Shōwa-dōri from JR Akihabara's Shōwa-dōri exit and walk about 8 minutes toward Ueno (465 m from Akihabara); 8 minutes from Suehirochō (Tokyo Metro Ginza line, exit 1).
hours_raw: 月・火・木・金・土・日 11:00 - 15:00／祝日 11:00 - 20:00／水 定休日　※スープ無くなり次第終了 — these were the hours until the 24 February 2026 closure.
gf_detail: Moot now that the shop is shut, and it would have been 'no' anyway: the whole menu was wheat ramen noodles in shōyu, shio and miso broths, all of which are built on wheat soy sauce or on a miso that is nowhere stated to be rice-only. No gluten-free claim ever appeared on Tabelog or in any coverage.
vegan_detail: No plant-based option. A shokudō ramen counter running animal stock, with chāshū on the standard bowls; the shop closed before any vegan item was ever recorded.

roles: 店主 (owner-chef, unnamed in any published source)
chef_bio.origin: Taitō 1-chōme, Taitō-ku — the shop stood on the far side of Shōwa-dōri from Akihabara, right on the Chiyoda/Taitō boundary
chef_bio.background: 粋な一生 opened on 12 December 2005 and ran for twenty years as an 18-seat ramen shokudō (10 counter, 8 table) under an aged hand-painted sign reading ラーメン食堂「粋な一生」. It reached Tabelog 3.71 and was described locally as one of the shops that defined Akihabara ramen, even though it sat far enough off the station that people crossed Shōwa-dōri specifically for it. The closing notice taped to the door read 「誠に勝手ながら、当店は令和8年2月24日をもちまして閉店することと致しました。これまで20年間、多くのお客様に温かく支えていただき、営業を続けることが出来ました。心より感謝申し上げます。」 No successor shop or relocation has been announced.
chef_bio.specialty: 塩ラーメン and 味噌ラーメン (¥900, butter ¥120 / corn ¥120) were the two bowls regulars named most; a 塩つけ麺 also had a following.

anecdotes.text: The closing notice thanked customers for twenty years: 「これまで20年間、多くのお客様に温かく支えていただき、営業を続けることが出来ました。」
Local reaction was almost entirely about the shio and the miso — 「ここの塩ラーメンと塩つけ麺が好きで、よく食べてたので残念…」 and 「アキバを代表するラーメン店の１つが」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13021102 is headed 【閉店】粋な一生（いきないっしょう）, files it under 秋葉原/ラーメン・つけ麺, and gives 東京都台東区台東1-27-2 竹善ビル1F, coordinates 35.70165/139.77677, 18 seats, cash only, all non-smoking, an opening date of 2005年12月12日, hours 11:00–15:00 (holidays to 20:00) closed Wednesdays with スープ無くなり次第終了, and a 3.71 rating. The Akihabara local blog ツルミロボBlog (kaztsu.com), posted 20 January 2026, photographs the closure notice and quotes it verbatim: final day 令和8年2月24日, after twenty years. It also prices the miso ramen at ¥900 with ¥120 butter and ¥120 corn toppings.

gf_cross_contamination.text: An 18-seat counter shokudō with a single noodle boiler serving nothing but wheat ramen; no separate preparation was ever claimed.

cultural_comfort.note: Do not send anyone here. 粋な一生 served its last bowl on 24 February 2026 after twenty years, and the notice on the door was a straight closure, not a move — no relocation or successor shop has been announced anywhere. The record should be hidden from the app.

enrich_note: Confirmed as a real Akihabara-area shop and confirmed permanently closed. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 粋な一生 (the double-encoded rstLst form that /rst/rstsearch/?sk= redirects to, HTTP 200, 96件) returns exactly one restaurant with the name, 13021102, and its page is already headed 【閉店】. The light record's 塩ラーメン and 秋葉原 both check out — the shop is 465 m from Akihabara's Shōwa-dōri exit, matching the sweep's neighbourhood string, and shio was one of its two signature bowls. The closure date comes from a photograph of the shop's own notice on the Akihabara local blog ツルミロボBlog (20 January 2026): 「令和8年2月24日をもちまして閉店」. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's own (35.701651, 139.776769), about 470 m from the sweep's approximate pin. Status closed_permanently with closed_since set; recommend hiding from the app.

name: 割烹たなか
address_ja: 〒101-0025 東京都千代田区神田佐久間町1-16 大橋ビル 1F
cuisine: A kappō running two completely different services: at lunch a queue for the 魚がし丼 (about ¥1,100) — big, thick-cut sashimi over rice eaten with the house sesame dare, sold until it runs out — and in the evening a proper counter-and-tatami kappō where reviewers' bills land at ¥6,000–¥7,999.
neighborhood: Kanda-Sakumachō 1-chōme, Chiyoda-ku — 96 m from Akihabara station's Shōwa-dōri exit (JR Yamanote, Keihin-Tōhoku, Chūō-Sōbu and Tsukuba Express), about 350 m from Iwamotochō (Toei Shinjuku line).
hours_raw: [月~金] 11:30～なくなり次第終了／17:00～22:30　定休日：土曜日・日曜日・祝日、水曜日はランチ休業
gf_detail: Nothing published either way, and the signature dish is a problem: the 魚がし丼 is dressed in a ゴマダレ, and a Japanese sesame dare is normally built on wheat shōyu — no gluten-free tamari is claimed anywhere. Tempura and simmered dishes on the evening kappō menu are the usual wheat-batter and wheat-shōyu constructions. On the other hand this is a small kappō with a chef at the counter and reservations taken for dinner, so plain sashimi without the dare is the kind of thing that can be asked for in advance. Treat it as ask-at-booking, not as a shop with a gluten-free line.
vegan_detail: A seafood house. Tabelog's genre string is 日本料理、海鮮、海鮮丼, the lunch service is a single sashimi bowl, and the dashi behind everything else will be katsuo. No vegetable-only course is advertised and nothing suggests one exists.

roles: 板前・店主 (owner-chef; not named in any source found)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Sakumachō, Chiyoda-ku — a ground-floor unit in the Ōhashi building, one block off Shōwa-dōri behind Akihabara station
chef_bio.background: 割烹たなか is a 20-seat kappō (6 counter, 10 on the tatami, 4 at tables) tucked behind Akihabara station on the Shōwa-dōri side, and it is known locally for a lunch that has nothing to do with the electronics district: the 魚がし丼, a bowl of large, thickly cut sashimi over rice served with the house sesame dare for about ¥1,100, sold weekdays from 11:30 until it runs out. Lunch is walk-in only — the shop takes no lunch bookings — and there is no Wednesday lunch. In the evening it works as a conventional kappō, closed weekends and public holidays, with cards accepted (JCB, AMEX, Diners) and private hire possible; reviewers' evening spend clusters at ¥6,000–¥7,999 against a ¥1,000–¥1,999 lunch. Tabelog rates it 3.55.
chef_bio.specialty: 魚がし丼 — the sashimi-over-rice lunch bowl with sesame dare, about ¥1,100.

anecdotes.text: A TikTok clip of the lunch bowl (@tokyo_foods, May 2023) has been viewed about 151,000 times and repeats the house line: 「ランチ営業時間 月・火・木・金 11:30～売り切れ次第ランチ終了／定休日 土・日・祝／◆魚がし丼1100」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13026551 gives 割烹たなか at 東京都千代田区神田佐久間町1-16 大橋ビル1F, tel 03-3253-5152, coordinates 35.69776/139.77462, 96 m from Akihabara station, genre 日本料理・海鮮・海鮮丼, weekday-only hours 11:30 until sold out and 17:00–22:30, closed Sat/Sun/holidays with no Wednesday lunch, reservations for dinner but not lunch, 6 counter + 10 tatami + 4 table seats, all non-smoking, cards accepted, rating 3.55. gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen information is published and no gluten-free preparation is claimed. A small kappō kitchen frying tempura in the evening shares its space with everything else on the menu.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature 魚がし丼 is served with a ゴマダレ, normally built on ordinary wheat soy sauce; the shop names no tamari or wheat-free seasoning.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Filed by Tabelog as 日本料理・海鮮・海鮮丼 with a raw-fish bowl as the only lunch; no plant-based option is listed.

cultural_comfort.level: Easy at lunch, book for dinner
cultural_comfort.note: Ninety seconds from Akihabara's Shōwa-dōri exit, which is exactly where the light record put it. Lunch is walk-in only and no reservations are taken, so go before the bowl sells out; there is no Wednesday lunch, and the shop is closed all weekend and on public holidays. Dinner takes reservations on 03-3253-5152 and accepts JCB, AMEX and Diners, but lunch is effectively cash-and-go and the counter is small. No English menu is advertised and there is no website, so a phone call in Japanese — or asking a hotel to call — is the only way to raise a dietary request before you arrive.

enrich_note: Confirmed, and it is genuinely the shop the sweep meant. The other twelve are in Niigata, Nagasaki, Mie, Gifu, Ishikawa, Aichi, Kanagawa, Toyama and Ehime, plus 割烹 多なか in Adachi-ku. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.697764, 139.774617). name: つじ田 神田御茶ノ水店
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町1-4 和田ビル 1F
cuisine: The original つじ田 — the shop that opened here in 2005 and made 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 a Tokyo genre. Sixteen counter seats, thick noodles into a heavy pork-and-dried-fish dip, finished at the table with sudachi and coarse black pepper; ¥1,000–¥1,999, no reservations, served until it runs out.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 1-chōme — 27 m from Ogawamachi station (Toei Shinjuku line): out of exit A7 and 40 m to the left. The same exits serve Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line) and Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), and JR Ochanomizu is a short walk north.
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 11:00 - 23:00／土・日・祝日 11:00 - 21:00　■ 売り切れ次第終了　■ 定休日：不定休
gf_detail: Ruled out by the operator's own allergen statement, not just by inference. つじ田's parent オイシーズ株式会社 (Oishes) publishes a group allergy page saying 「当店の厨房設備及び商品の製造上、アレルギー食材を完全に除くことができません」, that every dish is cooked with the same utensils so ingredients not belonging to a dish can transfer, and that 「麺、スープ等の製造工場では、小麦、卵、乳成分を原材料とする商品の製造を行ってます」 — the noodle and soup plant itself handles wheat, egg and dairy. It adds that the company may decline to serve customers who react to trace amounts. On top of that the product is wheat tsukemen noodles in a wheat-shōyu-based dip. There is no gluten-free item.
vegan_detail: Not possible. The house broth is the 豚骨魚介 double soup — pork bone plus dried fish — and the standard bowl carries chāshū. No plant-based or vegetable bowl appears on the brand's menu.

roles: 創業者・店主 (founder; the brand is operated by オイシーズ株式会社 / Oishes Inc.)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Ogawamachi, Chiyoda-ku — this shop is the brand's birthplace
chef_bio.background: つじ田 opened at Kanda-Ochanomizu in 2005 and is the shop the company itself credits with leading Tokyo's tsukemen culture: 「味から絆へ、2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来、味へ圧倒的なこだわりで東京のつけ麺文化を牽引」. From this 16-seat counter the brand grew into a nationwide group — Kōjimachi, Shinbashi, Iidabashi, Nihonbashi-Yaesu, Shibuya Fukuras, Suidōbashi, Ningyōchō, Ōtemachi One, Kachidoki, Tōyōchō, Ikebukuro, Osaka Higobashi and Expocity, and Fukuoka airport — plus two spin-off lines, つじ田 味噌の章 (a miso-ramen specialist opened in Ogawamachi in 2009, three Tokyo shops) and 成都正宗担々麺 (a tantanmen specialist opened in Ogawamachi in 2016). The stated house principle is that the recipe is never finished: 「濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺のパイオニアであるつじ田のこだわりは、常においしさを求めて進化を続けること」. The Kanda-Ochanomizu shop stays deliberately plain — counter only, cash with no electronic money, no reservations, unpredictable closing days, and it stops when the soup goes.
chef_bio.philosophy: 常においしさを求めて進化を続けること — keep evolving in pursuit of flavour; 「こだわりがあるからこそ、はじめてお客様に愛される」.
chef_bio.specialty: 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 — the thick pork-and-fish tsukemen the brand pioneered, eaten with sudachi and coarse black pepper.

anecdotes.text: The company dates the whole tsukemen brand to this address: 「2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来、味へ圧倒的なこだわりで東京のつけ麺文化を牽引」.
Tabelog's directions are unusually precise about how close it is — out of Ogawamachi exit A7, turn left, 40 m; the station is 27 m away.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13020599 lists つじ田 神田御茶ノ水店 at 東京都千代田区神田小川町1-4 和田ビル1F, tel 03-5256-3200, coordinates 35.69522/139.76651, genre つけ麺・ラーメン, 16 counter seats, 予約不可, no cards and no electronic money, all non-smoking, hours 11:00–23:00 weekdays and 11:00–21:00 weekends/holidays with 売り切れ次第終了 and 不定休, budget ¥1,000–¥1,999, rating 3.47, homepage tsukemen-tsujita.com. The brand site confirms the 2005 Kanda-Ochanomizu founding, the 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 identity, and the two sister brands (味噌の章 from 2009, 成都正宗担々麺 from 2016), both also started in Ogawamachi. The operator's allergy page at oishes.com/allergy states that allergens cannot be fully excluded, that shared utensils are used, that the noodle and soup factories handle wheat, egg and dairy, and that service may be refused to highly sensitive customers.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The operator states outright that allergens cannot be fully excluded and that the same utensils are used across the menu, so ingredients not belonging to a dish can transfer during cooking.
The noodle and soup factories that supply the shops also produce items made with wheat, egg and dairy.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A 濃厚豚骨魚介 tsukemen dip built in the ordinary way on wheat soy sauce; no tamari or gluten-free seasoning is named anywhere on the brand site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The defining broth is pork bone plus dried fish, and the standard bowl is served with chāshū.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The company publishes per-brand allergen tables for つじ田 (alongside 金子半之助 and 田中そば) behind an acknowledgement screen, and explicitly warns it may decline to serve customers who react to trace amounts.

positives.text: Allergen information is published brand by brand and kept current, which is more than most independent ramen shops offer — useful for a wheat-tolerant diner avoiding egg or dairy.

cultural_comfort.level: Very easy — but cash, and a queue
cultural_comfort.note: Twenty-seven metres from Ogawamachi station, so it is essentially impossible to miss: exit A7, turn left. Sixteen counter seats, no reservations, and neither cards nor electronic money are accepted, so bring cash. It closes when the soup runs out and its closing days are 不定休 rather than fixed, so check the brand site or its social accounts before making a special trip. Ordering is counter service on effectively one dish, so no Japanese is needed; the table ritual — squeeze the sudachi, grind the pepper — is worth copying from the person next to you. If you are avoiding egg or dairy rather than wheat, the operator's allergy page at oishes.com/allergy is genuinely usable.

enrich_note: Confirmed exactly as recorded, branch suffix included. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for つじ田 (HTTP 200, 66件) lists つじ田 神田御茶ノ水店 as 13020599 at 東京都千代田区神田小川町1-4 和田ビル1F — matching the light record's 「小川町 / 御茶ノ水駅周辺」 — and the brand's own site confirms this address is where つじ田 started in 2005, which is why the record's 「濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺」 string is the company's own wording. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.695216, 139.766514), about 250 m from the sweep's approximate pin. gf_confidence is set to 'no' on the operator's published statement rather than on inference: オイシーズ株式会社's allergy page says allergens cannot be fully excluded, shared utensils are used, and the noodle and soup plants handle wheat, egg and dairy.

name: つけ麺 素家
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-24 大栄堂第２ビル 1F
cuisine: A ten-seat one-man tsukemen counter serving a deliberately retro 豚骨魚介 dip — thick straight Taisei-Shokuhin noodles, chāshū, menma, naruto and negi all sunk in the bowl — with the house trick being a 自家製りんご甘酢, a sweet apple vinegar you pour over the noodles before dipping. つけ麺 ¥1,100, らーめん ¥1,050, 油そば ¥1,050; 200 g regular and 300 g large cost the same.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 3-chōme — 313 m from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line); about 4 minutes from the shared B5 exit that also serves Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku line) and Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line). Look for the building with the acoustic-guitar shop en.guitar lit up behind its second-floor window; the shop is the ground floor, in the former premises of 一挙一会.
gf_detail: No. The shop sells three dishes and all three are wheat noodles — the tsukemen and abura-soba use 200–300 g of thick straight noodles made by 大成食品, and the dip is described by reviewers as a 豚骨魚介醤油 tare, i.e. wheat soy sauce. There is no allergen information, no gluten-free claim, one boiler and one person working the whole counter, so there is no separable line even in principle.
vegan_detail: No. The dip is a pork-bone-and-dried-fish broth and every bowl comes with chāshū, menma and naruto (fish cake) already in it; the side menu is a chāshū rice bowl. Nothing plant-based is offered.

roles: 店主 (owner-chef, works the shop single-handed)
chef_bio.origin: Trained at 麺彩房 — the Nakano ramen house whose 豚骨魚介 style he still cooks
chef_bio.background: 素家 is fifteen years old and on its third address. It opened in Asakusabashi on 1 December 2010 under an owner who came out of 麺彩房, moved to Iidabashi on 26 March 2019, and moved again to Kanda-Ogawamachi on 17 October 2025, taking over the ground-floor unit that used to be 一挙一会. The current shop is an irregular U-shaped counter of ten seats (3-1-3-3) wrapped around the kitchen, worked by the owner alone — reviewers single out how quietly courteous the service is for a one-man ramen counter. The bowl is unfashionably old-school: a thick, glossy pork-and-fish shōyu dip that a veteran reviewer recognised immediately as 麺彩房's, with the noodles supplied, as at 麺彩房, by 大成食品. The one flourish is on the table — alongside the fish powder, vinegar and S&B ichimi sits a house-made apple sweet-vinegar that the shop tells you to pour straight onto the noodles; it reads as apple juice with a faint tartness rather than as vinegar. Soup-thinning dashi is left on the table in a pot. Tabelog rates it 3.37 and the shop posts on X as @soyatsuke; there is no telephone number on file.
chef_bio.specialty: つけ麺 ¥1,100 — 200 g regular or 300 g large at the same price — eaten first plain, then with the 自家製りんご甘酢, then finished with the table-side soup-splitting dashi.

anecdotes.text: A long-running Tokyo ramen blogger arrived ten minutes before the evening opening on 20 October 2025, three days after the shop moved in, and was first in a queue of three. His verdict on the dip: 「まんまは『麺彩房』譲りの味わい。ノス感あるレトロな豚魚つけ麺ですが、大変丁寧にしっかりと作り込まれていてとっても美味しい」.
The house serving suggestion is unusual enough that reviewers make a point of it — pour the 自家製りんご甘酢 directly over the noodles before dipping: 「りんご甘酢は全然酸っぱくなくて、りんご果汁にほのかな酸味的な、糖度多めの甘酸っぱい味わい」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13315015 lists つけ麺 素家 under 新御茶ノ水/ラーメン at 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-24 大栄堂第２ビル1F, coordinates 35.69544/139.76286, 313 m from Shin-Ochanomizu, 10 seats, 予約不可, no telephone on file, cash only, hours 11:15–15:30 plus 18:00–20:00 on weekdays, 11:15–15:30 on Saturdays and closed Sundays and public holidays, opening date 2025年10月17日, official account x.com/soyatsuke, rating 3.37. The ramen blog 麺好い（めんこい）ブログ, visiting on 20 October 2025, supplies the shop's history (Asakusabashi 1 December 2010, Iidabashi 26 March 2019, Ogawamachi 17 October 2025), the owner's 麺彩房 background, the full price list (つけ麺1100円 / らーめん1050円 / 油そば1050円 / チャーシュー丼400円 / ライス150円), the portion sizes, the 10-seat U-shaped counter, the 大成食品 noodles, the table condiments including the house apple sweet-vinegar, and the landmark of the en.guitar shop upstairs. Retty also carries the shop under Kanda/Ogawamachi.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Ten seats, one boiler, one person cooking, and a menu of three wheat-noodle dishes. No allergen information is published and no wheat-free preparation is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The dip is described by reviewers as とろっと濃厚な豚骨魚介醤油味 — an ordinary wheat-shōyu tare. No tamari is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork-bone and dried-fish dip, with chāshū, menma and fish-cake naruto served inside the dip bowl itself; the soup-splitting liquid on the table is a bonito dashi.

cultural_comfort.level: Easy but tight — ticket machine, cash, ten seats
cultural_comfort.note: Buy a ticket from the machine as you walk in, then sit; the owner works alone so service is calm but there is no room to deliberate. Cash only, no reservations, ten seats, and it shuts between 15:30 and 18:00 on weekdays, closes at 15:30 on Saturdays and does not open at all on Sundays or public holidays — worth checking @soyatsuke on X before a special trip, since the shop has no telephone listed. Paper aprons are on a shelf by the door, self-service. Portions are the friendliest thing about it: 200 g and 300 g cost the same, so say 大盛 if you want it. No English menu.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「Tsukemen Soya」 with cuisine つけ麺 and neighbourhood 新御茶ノ水駅; the business is 「つけ麺 素家」, read そや, so the sweep had captured a romanisation rather than a garbling. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for そや (HTTP 200, 416件) surfaced つけ麺 素家 as the only tsukemen shop of that reading anywhere, at 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-24, filed by Tabelog under 新御茶ノ水 — the same station the light record names — and 313 m from it. A Yahoo Japan search for つけ麺 素家 小川町 新御茶ノ水 (HTTP 200) returned the Tabelog page, two independent visit reports and a Retty listing, all at the same address. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.695441, 139.762863), about 350 m from the sweep's approximate pin. Worth flagging for the app: this shop only moved here on 17 October 2025, so any older Iidabashi or Asakusabashi address for 素家 is stale.

name: お茶の水、大勝軒
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-1-5 須田ビル 1F
cuisine: A direct 暖簾分け of the vanished 東池袋大勝軒, run by a disciple who was told by Yamagishi himself never to change the taste — so the 特製もりそば here is the original tsukemen: hand-cut, chewy noodles chilled then dipped back in hot water, into a collagen-heavy sweet-sour-shōyu dip. It also serves a 1954 Shōwa-era curry that won the Kanda Curry Grand Prix, and from the afternoon a 復刻版 menu of dishes sealed away when the old shop closed. ¥1,000–¥1,999.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 3-chōme — 5 minutes from Jimbōchō (Toei Mita, Toei Shinjuku, Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines, 363 m), 5 minutes from Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku) and Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 6 minutes from JR Ochanomizu.
hours_raw: 11:00～21:00 ＜17時より復刻版（Classic）メニューもご提供します＞　定休日：月曜日（月曜日が祝日の場合は火曜日）、年始・お盆　※まれに貸切宴会のときがありますのでご注意下さい（SNSでお知らせあり）
gf_detail: No, on several counts at once. The noodles are wheat; the shop's own description of the 特製もりそば calls the dip a 醤油タレ with a sweet-sour edge, i.e. wheat soy sauce; the 復刻版カレー中華 is finished with 醤油だれ and 水溶き片栗粉 over the curry roux; and the celebrated curry is explicitly thickened 「小麦粉とスパイスで仕上げた」 — wheat flour in the roux itself. The gyōza wrappers are made in-house from wheat flour and the shop also serves wontons and shūmai. No allergen statement and no gluten-free item exists.
vegan_detail: No. The stock is the 丸長 lineage 中華そば broth — pork bone and chicken carcass with niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi layered over it, which is the shop's whole historical claim — so even the vegetable-forward 復刻版タンメン is built on animal and fish stock and stir-fried with pork. The house まかない飯 is chāshū fried with raw egg. Nothing plant-based is offered.

roles: 山岸一雄の弟子 (disciple of Kazuo Yamagishi, granted 暖簾分け)
chef_bio.origin: Minami-Ōtsuka, Toshima-ku — he grew up a short walk from the old Higashi-Ikebukuro Taishōken
chef_bio.background: The Taishōken line runs 丸長 (Ogikubo, 1948, founded by the Shinshū soba craftsman 青木勝治, who first put niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi into a Chinese-style broth) → 栄楽 → 中野大勝軒 (1951, named for the wish 「大きく軒並みに勝る」) → 東池袋大勝軒 (1961), where 山岸一雄 turned the staff-meal つけそば into the 特製もりそば of 1955 and, in doing so, invented tsukemen as a commercial dish. Over about twenty years Yamagishi granted around a hundred 暖簾分け, and their own disciples take the family past two hundred shops; the Higashi-Ikebukuro original closed in March 2007 to redevelopment and Yamagishi's failing health. 田内川真介 grew up in Minami-Ōtsuka and had been eating there since boyhood, treated by Yamagishi 「実の子供のように」; in 1995, aged eighteen and in his first year of university, he became the old shop's first-ever part-timer. He took a salaried job after graduating, quit it because he wanted to preserve Yamagishi's taste, and went back to be taken on as a formal apprentice. He was granted 暖簾分け after about eighteen months but kept training while he looked for premises, and opened お茶の水、大勝軒 in September 2006 with Yamagishi supervising the reconstruction of the old Higashi-Ikebukuro flavour. Yamagishi's parting words before opening — 「真介、おまえだけは味を変えるなよ。」 — are the shop's governing instruction, and it has since become one of the family's designated keepers of the 復刻版 (Classic) menu, reviving dishes the old shop had sealed away, reproduced to the original recipes under Yamagishi's own supervision. Its Shōwa-era curry, created by Yamagishi in 1954 at Nakano out of his memory of navy curry, took 準グランプリ at the 2016 神田カレーグランプリ and the outright グランプリ in 2017, with a further 準グランプリ and the Meister Prize in 2019 for a dry keema. The shop now anchors a small group including 大勝軒next and 山ノ内大勝軒 in Yamagishi's birthplace under Shiga Kōgen.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「真介、おまえだけは味を変えるなよ」 — Yamagishi's instruction not to change the taste. The shop treats that as covering not only Yamagishi's own cooking but the 栄楽 and 中野大勝軒 traditions behind it.
chef_bio.specialty: 特製もりそば — the original tsukemen, hand-cut chewy noodles chilled and then passed back through hot water so the dip stays hot; 復刻版タンメン, 復刻版カレー中華 (Yamagishi's own invention at twenty, from his father's navy curry), 復刻版ワンタン/ワンタンメン/シュウマイ and the all-day 餃子; the Kanda Curry Grand Prix-winning curry; and the まかない飯, block-cut chāshū fried with egg and spring onion.

anecdotes.text: Tsukemen exists because a customer looked over the counter. Yamagishi was eating the staff-meal つけそば out of sight in the kitchen when a regular said 「うまそうじゃないの。おれたちにも食わせてよ」; he tried it on a few people, the reaction was good, and it went on the menu in 1955 as 特製もりそば.
The dish began as thrift, not invention: in the post-war food shortage wheat flour was too precious to throw away, so 青木勝治 devised a way to eat the noodles left in the zaru 「ざるそば気分で」.
Tauchigawa was the old Higashi-Ikebukuro shop's first part-time employee, hired in 1995 at eighteen; he later quit a company job to come back as an apprentice.

The curry is older than the tsukemen — Yamagishi built it in 1954 as manager of Nakano Taishōken from his memory of the navy curry his father brought home, and it won the Kanda Curry Grand Prix outright in 2017.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13298962 lists お茶の水、大勝軒 at 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-1-5 須田ビル1F, tel 03-3291-9933, coordinates 35.69468/139.76208, genre つけ麺・ラーメン・カレー, 26 seats (10 counter, two tables of four, four of two), open 11:00–21:00 and closed Mondays, budget ¥1,000–¥1,999, ticket-machine self-service with electronic money and PayPay accepted at a terminal under the machine, rating 3.61, and an opening date of 2024年7月6日 for the present premises, noting the shop moved from 千代田区神田小川町3-1-5. The shop's own site taisho-ken.tokyo confirms the address, phone, 11:00–21:00 hours and the Monday closure (Tuesday when Monday is a public holiday, plus New Year and Obon), and carries three substantial pages: 大勝軒の歴史 (the 丸長 → 栄楽 → 中野 → 東池袋 lineage, the 1955 origin of 特製もりそば, the ~100 暖簾分け, the March 2007 closure of Higashi-Ikebukuro, and Tauchigawa's biography from 1995 part-timer to September 2006 opening), 味へのこだわり, and お品書き (the 復刻版 Classic menu, the 1954 curry and its Kanda Curry Grand Prix results in 2016/2017/2019, the in-house gyōza wrappers, and the まかない飯). Official accounts are facebook.com/taishouken.tokyo and instagram.com/ochanomizutaishouken; there is an online store at shopping.taisho-ken.tokyo.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One kitchen turning out wheat noodles, hand-made wheat gyōza and wontons, shūmai and a flour-thickened curry roux. No allergen information is published and no wheat-free preparation is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop describes the 特製もりそば dip as a 醤油タレ with a sweet-sour note — ordinary wheat soy sauce, with no tamari mentioned.
The 復刻版カレー中華 is finished by combining 醤油だれ, potato-starch slurry and spring onion in the soup before the curry roux goes on top.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The house broth is the 丸長 lineage stock — pork bone and chicken carcass with niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi — so fish is in the base of everything, including the vegetable-heavy 復刻版タンメン, which is also stir-fried with pork.
The 大勝軒 curry is made by frying pork, onion, carrot and potato in lard and simmering them in the ramen stock.

cultural_comfort.level: Welcoming and self-service — one of the easier famous shops
cultural_comfort.note: This is a ticket-machine shop with an unusual routine: buy the ticket, hand it to the kitchen, take back the stub, and collect your bowl yourself when your number is called. Water, garlic, the soup-splitting dashi and clearing your dishes are also self-service; pepper and a cloth are on each table. Unusually for a ramen counter it has 26 seats including proper tables, takes reservations, welcomes children, and accepts transport IC cards, nanaco, WAON, iD, QUICPay, PayPay and Merpay at a terminal under the ticket machine — but no credit cards. Closed Mondays (Tuesday instead when Monday is a public holiday) and over New Year and Obon, and it very occasionally shuts for a private party, announced on its Instagram. Note the timing on the 復刻版 Classic dishes: the shop's front page says they start at 17:00 while the menu page says 15:00, so if you are coming specifically for the tanmen or the curry-chūka, aim for the evening. No English menu, but the ticket machine and the one-dish nature of もりそば make it manageable.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「大勝軒 (Ochanomizu Taishoken BRANCHING)」 with neighbourhood 「九段下 / 御茶ノ水駅周辺」; the business is 「お茶の水、大勝軒」, and the stray English word BRANCHING is a translation of 暖簾分け — the term for the branch-off licence Yamagishi granted the owner, which the sweep evidently picked up from descriptive copy rather than from the shop's name. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 大勝軒 御茶ノ水 (HTTP 200) returned just 2件, of which one is this shop, 13298962; its own site taisho-ken.tokyo confirms the identity, the address and the 暖簾分け story. The record's 九段下 is wrong — the shop is in Kanda-Ogawamachi, nearest station Jimbōchō at 363 m, with Ochanomizu six minutes away — so the neighbourhood string has been rewritten. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.694675, 139.762080), about 250 m from the sweep's approximate pin. One thing a merge should not misread: Tabelog gives an opening date of 6 July 2024 and flags a move 「『千代田区神田小川町3-1-5』から移転」, but the business itself dates from September 2006 — the 2024 date is the current premises, not the shop.

name: 江戸富士
address_ja: 東京都文京区湯島2-7-7 光ビル 1F
cuisine: Eleven seats in a quiet stretch of Yushima where the lunchtime queue starts half an hour before opening: the 江戸富士バラ海鮮丼, about ¥2,100, is thick-cut sashimi piled over rice in a shallow bowl, with miso soup ¥350; the fish runs out and the shop shuts. In the evening it works as a sushi counter, where reviewers' bills reach ¥10,000–¥14,999.
neighborhood: Yushima 2-chōme, Bunkyō-ku, near the Japan Football Museum — 485 m and about 7 minutes from JR Ochanomizu (Chūō-Sōbu line), 6 minutes from Ochanomizu on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line, 8 minutes from Suehirochō (Tokyo Metro Ginza line) and about 10 minutes from Yushima (Chiyoda line).
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 11:30 - 14:00／土 12:00 - 14:00／日 定休日　■ ネタが無くなり次第終了　※臨時休業が多いので、電話にて営業確認することが必須
gf_detail: Nothing published either way, and this needs care rather than optimism. The core of the lunch is raw fish and rice, which is not itself a gluten problem, but sushi rice is seasoned with vinegar that is often blended with other seasonings, the soy sauce on the counter will be ordinary wheat shōyu unless the shop says otherwise, and the miso soup at ¥350 is very likely a wheat-containing awase or mugi miso — 麦味噌 is barley. Imitation-crab, tamagoyaki and any simmered anago glaze on a sushi counter all carry wheat as standard. There is no allergen information and no gluten-free claim, and the shop has no website on which to check. It is the kind of place where a chef at the counter could plate sashimi and rice without sauce if asked, so 'ask' rather than 'no' — but ask in Japanese, and ask about the shōyu specifically.
vegan_detail: A sushi and kaisendon house whose entire lunch service is one raw-fish bowl and whose Tabelog profile says 魚料理にこだわる. No vegetable-only or plant-based option is listed anywhere, and any dashi will be katsuo.

roles: 大将・店主 (owner-chef; builds the lunch bowls single-handed)
chef_bio.origin: Yushima 2-chōme, Bunkyō-ku — a ground-floor unit in a residential block behind the Japan Football Museum
chef_bio.background: 江戸富士 is an eleven-seat shop — a seven-seat counter and two tables of four — that behaves like two businesses. Lunch, Monday to Saturday, is a single item: the 江戸富士バラ海鮮丼, thick, generous cuts of sashimi over rice, about ¥2,100, with miso soup at ¥350. It is popular enough that a visitor arriving thirty minutes before opening in December 2023 found roughly fifteen people already waiting — in a queue hidden down the alley to the left of the shop rather than in front of it — and was not seated until about 11:50. The owner makes the bowls alone and the service stops when the fish is gone. In the evening the same room is a sushi-ya with sake the shop takes seriously, reservations accepted, private hire for up to twenty, and a spend that reviewers put at ¥10,000–¥14,999. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB) are taken at dinner only — lunch is cash. Tabelog rates it 3.54 and warns in its own notes that unscheduled closures are frequent enough that phoning ahead on 03-3811-0111 is essential.
chef_bio.specialty: 江戸富士バラ海鮮丼 (about ¥2,100) — the thick-cut sashimi bowl that the lunch queue forms for; add the ¥350 miso soup.

anecdotes.text: The queue is not where you expect it. A December 2023 visitor arrived half an hour early, saw nobody in front of the shop and thought she was first — the fifteen people ahead of her were lined up out of sight in the alley to the left.
Same visit: the room held a broad mix of ages and included Korean tourists, and although the menu is Japanese only, the staff worked through it with gestures rather than turning anyone away.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13071145 lists 江戸富士 under 御茶ノ水/寿司・海鮮丼 at 東京都文京区湯島2-7-7 光ビル1F, tel 03-3811-0111, coordinates 35.70402/139.76529, 485 m from JR Ochanomizu with the Japan Football Museum given as the landmark, 11 seats (7 counter, 4 table), lunch 11:30–14:00 weekdays and 12:00–14:00 Saturdays, closed Sundays, ネタが無くなり次第終了, evening reservations accepted, private hire up to 20, VISA/Master/JCB but not at lunch, all non-smoking, 日本酒にこだわる and 魚料理にこだわる, dinner budget ¥5,000–¥5,999 (reviewers ¥10,000–¥14,999) against a ¥2,000–¥2,999 lunch, rating 3.54, and an explicit warning that 臨時休業 are frequent so ringing to confirm is essential. An independent visit report at amarettoo.com (December 2023) gives the bowl's name and price (江戸富士バラ海鮮丼 ¥2,100 incl. tax, 味噌汁 ¥350), the pre-opening queue, the hidden side-alley line, the seat count, the single-owner service and the Japanese-only handwritten menu by the door.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen information is published, there is no website, and one chef builds every bowl in an eleven-seat room. Nothing wheat-free is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A sushi and kaisendon counter with no stated tamari; the shōyu on the table should be assumed to be ordinary wheat soy sauce, and the ¥350 miso soup is not specified as rice-miso.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The lunch service is a single raw-fish bowl and Tabelog records the shop as 魚料理にこだわる; there is no plant-based item.

positives.text: Staff have been observed working patiently through the Japanese-only menu with foreign visitors by gesture rather than turning them away, which is a good sign for making a dietary request understood in person.

cultural_comfort.level: Friendly, but you have to work for the seat
cultural_comfort.note: Phone first — Tabelog's own notes say unscheduled closures are frequent and that confirming by telephone (03-3811-0111) is essential, and there is no website or social account to check instead. For lunch arrive well before 11:30 and look for the queue in the alley to the LEFT of the shop, not in front of it; the fish runs out and the shop closes at 14:00 regardless. Lunch is cash only — the cards (VISA, Master, JCB) are dinner-only — and there is no English menu, only a handwritten Japanese one by the entrance, though staff have a good record of getting through it with gestures. It is a 7-minute walk from JR Ochanomizu through a residential stretch of Yushima near the Japan Football Museum, so allow more time than the distance suggests. Dinner is a different and much more expensive proposition: book, and expect ¥10,000 and up.

enrich_note: Confirmed. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 江戸富士 (HTTP 200, 84件) returns exactly two restaurants with that exact name — this one, 13071145, and an unrelated 江戸富士 in Aichi (23088069) — and the Tokyo one is at 文京区湯島2-7-7, filed under 御茶ノ水 with the genre 寿司・海鮮丼. That matches all three of the light record's fields: 湯島, 御茶ノ水駅周辺, and 海鮮丼・寿司. A Yahoo Japan search for 江戸富士 湯島 海鮮丼 店主 (HTTP 200) returned four independent visit write-ups plus the Tabelog review index, all at the same address, one of which supplies the bowl's name and price. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.704023, 139.765287), about 530 m north of the sweep's approximate pin. No website exists — Tabelog lists none and none of the write-ups link one — so website and menu_url are left null rather than guessed. gf_confidence is 'ask' rather than 'options': raw fish over rice is superficially promising, but nothing is published about the shōyu, the sushi-rice seasoning or the miso, and the shop cannot be checked in advance except by telephone in Japanese.
